attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, given as one item in his list of things OpenAI must do to survive.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'hypothesizing' framing, the two-year survival condition, the scope (GPT or a successor) and the loose magnitude. It is really a necessary-condition claim: if OpenAI survived, the breakthrough must have happened.

contract.note: Reading 'thousands of percent' as an enormous multiple, screened at roughly 10x, is a fair, ordinary reading. Requiring comparable internal costs and excluding API prices is reasonable. Requiring both building and operating costs matches his words.

evidence.note: Dated October 2026 release shows OpenAI still operating, so the survival condition is met. It says nothing about the cost reduction.
OpenAI's own disclosure of a 20% cut in serving costs from kernel work. One partial improvement; no cumulative baseline and nothing on development costs.
Independent data on falling customer inference prices across providers, up to March 2025. Prices, not OpenAI's internal costs.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI survived past July 29, 2026, so the claim can be checked: did a breakthrough cut both development and operating costs by an enormous factor? The packet has only a 20% serving-cost gain disclosed by OpenAI and industry-wide price declines. There is no comparable series of internal costs, so it neither confirms nor rules out the required reduction.

attribution.note: Zitron's own stated belief in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'I believe... has to raise' is firm language. The proposition leaves out the timing after Microsoft's earnings, but the contract restores it. The 'more realistic case' framing is kept as a qualifier.

contract.note: Testing whether a new primary raise happened by January 29, 2025, after Microsoft's July 30 earnings, is a fair, ordinary reading. Treating 'within' as an outer deadline is reasonable. The contract correctly sets aside the stronger claim that the raise was strictly necessary.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own dated announcement of $6.6B in new funding on October 2, 2024. It is issuer confirmation of the financing, as the contract requires.
Dated transcript showing Microsoft's earnings call on July 30, 2024, before the raise.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI completed $6.6B of new funding on October 2, 2024. That is after Microsoft's July 30 earnings and well before the January 29, 2025 deadline, so the financing forecast came true. Whether the raise was strictly necessary is not tested.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter; 'I believe will' is his own forecast.

semantics.note: Keeps both parts, the huge round and the investor types with their equity cost, and keeps 'I believe'. Firm language, so it is scored. No deadline was given.

contract.note: Treating the investor types as alternatives and 'swaths of equity' as a substantial ownership stake is a fair, ordinary reading. Requiring disclosed terms for the equity part is demanding but consistent with his words.

evidence.note: Confirms a major $6.6B round in October 2024. No ownership terms.
Reuters (syndicated) reports large funds such as Fidelity, SoftBank and MGX in the round, via convertible notes. It gives no equity amounts.
SoftBank says it holds about 11% of OpenAI in total after its 2025 investments. This is total ownership, not the stake given up in any one round.

reviews.rationale: Huge rounds did happen, and large investment funds took part, so those parts are consistent with the forecast. But no disclosed terms show the substantial equity given up in a specific round, which the contract requires. With no deadline and no conclusive event, the combined forecast is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assessment in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Years from delivering' at OpenAI scale is a firm claim about delivery timing. The 'iterative' label is fairly left out as commentary.

contract.note: Plural 'years' as at least two years, and OpenAI scale as enough for a substantial OpenAI workload, are fair, ordinary readings. Limiting comparable suppliers to proven equivalents is reasonable, since he described chips built for single models.

evidence.note: Etched's own June 30, 2026 release: production still ramping, first rack still being validated with customers, gigawatt scale targeted for 2027. No delivery at scale.
Etched's August 2026 release: the first single rack went to Jane Street in July 2026. Far below OpenAI scale by the checkpoint.
Cerebras powered a limited OpenAI research preview, with capacity still ramping. Different kind of supplier; scale not shown.
Cerebras capacity for OpenAI is planned in tranches through 2028. This is future capacity, not deliveries.

reviews.rationale: Etched only shipped its first single customer rack in July 2026, about two years after the post, and was still ramping production with gigawatt scale aimed at 2027. It did not deliver at OpenAI scale within two years. Cerebras ran only a limited OpenAI preview, does not clearly fit his 'single-model' description, and its scale was not shown, so it does not contradict the claim.
